phases.name: Heat & Platinum
phases.goal: Crime-spree cleanup, the last counts, 100% completion — then the platinum pops itself.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.keyFact: No work of its own — it pops by itself the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned.
trophies.guide: This one unlocks on its own the moment every other trophy is banked, so there is nothing to chase directly. Work the roadmap in order — story, strangers, activities, then the crime cleanup — and keep a manual save at each phase boundary so a missed flag never costs a second playthrough.
steps: There is nothing to do here directly: the platinum unlocks automatically once the other 54 trophies are all in your collection. [1] [2]
Follow the roadmap order — story first, stranger strands and activities in the middle, crime cleanup last — because the 100% gold, A Long Road, is the real final gate ahead of it. [3] [4]
Keep a manual save at every phase boundary, so one missed flag never turns into a whole second playthrough. [3] [5]

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.keyFact: Gone Fishing opens the game — the first trophy almost every player will earn.
trophies.guide: Play through the opening mission Gone Fishing and the trophy pops as it ends. It is the game's first mission, so it lands naturally for nearly everyone; if it somehow fails to award, replay the mission from the pause menu and finish it cleanly.
steps: Just play Gone Fishing through to its end and this trophy pops on its own; nothing here can be missed. [1] [2]
It opens the game, which is why almost every player earns it first — the first main mission of Chapter 1. [4] [6]
If a replay ever fails to award it, run the mission again from the pause menu and finish it cleanly. [5] [7]

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.keyFact: Chapter 1 finished — a milestone on the story road, not a skill test.
trophies.guide: See every story mission in Chapter 1 through to the chapter-end screen. The trophy actually pops once the first mission of Chapter 2 begins, so keep pushing the main story and save the long side detours for later phases.
steps: Work through every story mission in Chapter 1 until the chapter-end screen appears, and this trophy lands. [1] [2]
Chapters follow one another in strict order, so this is a milestone rather than a challenge — it pops after you finish What's in the Bag?, the first mission of Chapter 2. [6] [3]
Keep the main missions moving and leave the long side detours for the later phases, where the roadmap gives them room. [3] [5]

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.keyFact: Chapter 2 finished — the same deal as Chapter 1: see the chapter through.
trophies.guide: Play Chapter 2's story missions in order until the chapter closes. Like the previous chapter trophy, it pops when the next chapter's first mission starts — a milestone, not a test — so a save at the chapter start is optional insurance.
steps: Chapter 2 plays exactly like Chapter 1: take its story missions in order until the chapter closes, and the trophy follows. [1] [2]
It pops after Welcome to Vice City, the first main mission of Chapter 3, so the chapter boundary is easy to spot. [6] [3]
A save at the chapter's start is cheap insurance if you want one, but the trophy itself asks only for completion. [3] [4]

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.keyFact: Chapter 3 finished — keep the story moving; side content can wait.
trophies.guide: Clear Chapter 3's story missions in sequence and the trophy follows once the first two missions of Chapter 4 are done. Side content you pass stays available in free roam afterwards, so there is no penalty for pressing on.
steps: Clear Chapter 3 by finishing its story missions in order. [1] [2]
It pops after the first two main missions of Chapter 4, Ocean Beach and Another Life. [6] [3]
Whatever you pass by stays waiting in free roam afterwards, so pressing on costs you nothing. [3] [4]

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.keyFact: The last full chapter done — the finale is next.
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 4's story missions in order; the trophy pops after the chapter's final mission. Bank a manual save there — this is the last full chapter before the finale — and use the open map to clear stranger strands and activities before moving on.
steps: Finish Chapter 4's story missions in order and the trophy follows. [1] [2]
It pops after Starting From Zero, the last main mission of Chapter 4, so bank a manual save here — Chapter 4 is the last full chapter before the finale. [6] [3]
Before you move past it, clear the stranger strands and activities you care about: cleanup is far easier with the whole map already open. [4] [7]

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.window: Final mission ONLY — once the credits roll, the finale cannot be replayed; there is no mission replay.
trophies.saveAdvice: Keep a manual save before you attempt this one — finish the open-world cleanup first, then start the finale.
trophies.keyFact: Gold for finishing the final mission — tidy up the open world first, with a save in hand.
trophies.guide: Before the finale, make a manual save and finish your open-world cleanup — collectibles, stranger strands and partner trophies are all easier with the full story still open. Then play the final mission through; afterwards you continue in free roam, but there is no mission replay.
steps: Make a manual save first and keep it — that save is your insurance if anything in the finale locks a flag away. [3] [4]
Before you start the final mission, finish the open-world cleanup the roadmap lists: collectibles, stranger strands and partner trophies are all simpler with the full story still open. [4] [5]
Then play the mission through to its end and this gold pops; after the story you continue in free roam, but there is no mission replay. [4] [7]

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.keyFact: Story mission Breakfast Run — it pops the moment the mission ends.
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run when the story offers it. Named-mission trophies ask only for a finish — no grade, time or style requirement — so play it however you like and move on.
steps: Finish the story mission Breakfast Run and this trophy is yours. [1] [2]
Named-mission trophies like this one are pure progress markers: take the mission when the story offers it, and the trophy follows the finish. [3] [4]
The description sets no grade, time or style requirement, so play it however suits you and move on. [1] [5]

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.keyFact: Story mission The Cartel Heist — it pops the moment the mission ends.
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist, which arrives in the story's own order after its setup missions. The heist hits the Sinfrontera National Bank in Tequesta for $120,000; save the heist-flavoured side content — vaults and armored trucks — for the Phase 5 cleanup.
steps: Finish the story mission The Cartel Heist — it turns up in the story's own order, so there is nothing to unlock beforehand. [1] [2]

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.keyFact: Story mission Child's Play — it pops the moment the mission ends.
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play. Like the other named-mission trophies it only asks for a finish, so tick it off in the tracker as you work through Phase 1's story spine.
steps: Finish the story mission Child's Play. [1] [2]
Like the other named-mission trophies, it asks only for a finish — no medal, no particular approach. [3] [4]
Tick it off in the tracker as you go: the story trophies form the spine of Phase 1. [3] [5]

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.keyFact: Story mission Headliners — it pops the moment the mission ends.
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. No extra condition hides in the description — finish the mission and it is yours — and by then most of the map and activity types should be open for Phase 3.
steps: Finish the story mission Headliners. [1] [2]
The description hides no extra condition — complete the mission and the trophy is yours. [1] [3]
By the time Headliners is done, the map and most activity types should be open, and Phase 3 is ready to begin. [3] [4]

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.keyFact: The VCIA Takedown mission at the airport — its neighbour is Catch Me If You Can.
trophies.guide: Complete the VCIA Takedown mission at the airport — a Chapter 4 job with a long run of prep missions that closes the chapter's heist arc. Finish the mission itself first; the unscheduled departure for Catch Me If You Can is a separate attempt outside it.
steps: The VCIA Takedown mission takes you to the airport, and finishing it is all this trophy wants. [1] [2]

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.keyFact: Story mission Operation Savage Glory — heavy combat, but only a finish is asked.
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory. It sounds like a heavy-combat set piece, so arrive with your best weapons and armour, but the trophy only asks for a finish — treat it as a story beat and Phase 1's named-mission set is done.
steps: Operation Savage Glory sounds like a heavy-combat set piece — turn up with your best weapons and armour. [1] [2]
The trophy itself only asks you to finish the mission, so treat it as a story beat rather than a test. [3] [4]

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.keyFact: Gold for 100% completion — the last obstacle before the platinum itself.
trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion on the game's own checklist — 35 lines in three groups, visible under Progress after the story, though story progress already counts. The checklist is lenient, roughly 60% of true game completion, but eleven lines demand everything, so plan around robberies, underwater discoveries, ranges, drone races and Bret's target decks first.
steps: This gold pops when you reach 100% completion, and nothing else stands between the two. [1] [2]

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.keyFact: Silver: 250 stunts across the playthrough — let the total grow, then mop up.
trophies.guide: Land 250 stunts of any kind — jumps, near misses, drifts, air time — all counting toward one total that never resets. Most will happen on their own through the story and free roam; mop up the rest late in Phase 3 at repeatable jump spots, and race alongside it, since races hand you stunts for free.
steps: Two hundred and fifty stunts is the target, and every kind counts toward the same total: jumps, near misses, drifts, air time. [1] [2]
The counter never resets, so there is no rush — most of it will happen on its own through story missions and free roam. [3] [5]
Whatever remains, clean up late in Phase 3 at jump spots you can repeat; the game holds 397 stunts in all, and 100% asks for 300 of them. [4] [7]

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.keyFact: One try at each of the 9 activity types — a sampler, not a slog.
trophies.guide: Try each of the nine activity types once: fishing, hunting, golf, a shooting range, pool, basketball, an arcade game, a race win and a stunt. A single attempt at each is enough, so treat it as a taster tour of Phase 3 and tick types off as you sample them.
steps: Nine activity types, one try each — that is the whole ask. [1] [2]
The nine are fishing, hunting, golf, a shooting range, pool, basketball, an arcade game, winning a race, and a stunt. [6] [3]
One attempt each is enough, which makes this a taster tour of Phase 3 rather than a grind; tick each type off as you sample it. [6] [4]

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.keyFact: Silver: gold medals across all 42 range challenges — every last one.
trophies.guide: Earn gold in all 42 Shooting Range challenges — 18 at Griffin and 24 at Rodgers Ranch — buying the $5 waiver pass from each range's clerk before the challenges appear. Learn each weapon's recoil and work through the list a few challenges at a time; ranges also raise Focus, which makes Gunslinger easier.
steps: Gold medals in every Shooting Range challenge — all 42 of them, and 100% needs all 42 as well. [1] [2]

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.keyFact: A drone race win at each of the 14 Top Fun spots.
trophies.guide: Win a drone race at each of the 14 Top Fun locations — some charge an entry fee. Each location holds three races, 42 in all, with the third unlocked by beating par in the first two; drones reward a clean line over raw speed, so learn a course's corners before racing it flat out.
steps: Fourteen locations, one drone race win at each — some charge an entry fee. [1] [2]

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.keyFact: Twenty race wins, each on a different race — no repeats.
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — repeats of a favourite do not count. There are 40 unique races, shown as blue icons within about 100 metres and filterable under Map, Activities, Racing; rotate through the list with a fast, stable car, and the extra ten wins for 100% come free while you finish the set.
steps: Twenty race wins, and the key word is different — winning your favourite race twenty times earns you nothing here. [1] [2]
There are 40 unique races, shown as blue icons once you are within about 100 metres; filter them under Map, then Activities, then Racing. [7] [6]
Rotate through the race list, keep a note of the wins you have banked, and pick a fast, stable car you trust. [3] [5]

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.keyFact: One fishing win against Cal — a single rival to beat.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a single fishing challenge. Watch the line tension, reel in the windows the game gives you, and never rush the catch; losing costs nothing but the attempt, so keep going until the win lands.
steps: One rival, one win: beat Cal at a fishing challenge. [1] [2]

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.keyFact: Any single arcade game played to its end screen — the quickest activity tick.

trophies.saveAdvice: Keep a manual save before you attempt this one — accept Lucia's balcony meditation in Chapter 1; it may not come back.

Do the Chapter 1 balcony session first — after Down to Earth, talk to Lucia in the kitchen, follow her to the balcony and choose Accept — because it vanishes when Chapter 1 ends and may be required; then work the nine free-roam spots in map order, with the Mount Kalaga ascent unlocking last.

dispute.topic: Is the Chapter 1 balcony meditation required for the trophy?

a.text: Required: you need all 18, so do the balcony session in Chapter 1 or lose the trophy.

b.text: Possibly unneeded: the balcony adds +1 but is not marked as a spot; the final meditation may count double.

dispute.call: Our call: do it in Chapter 1 anyway — two minutes, free insurance.

disputes.topic: Is any trophy missable at all?
disputes.a: Only 1 possibly missable: Positive Mental Attitude (PowerPyx, KeenGamer).
disputes.b: None known: Push Square lists 0 missable trophies.
disputes.call: Our call: treat PMA as possibly missable — one 2-minute balcony session in Chapter 1 removes the whole risk.

disputes.topic: Is the Chapter 1 balcony meditation required for the trophy?
disputes.a: Required: all 18 meditations, do the balcony in Chapter 1 (Beebom, KeenGamer, GameTrek).
disputes.b: Possibly unneeded: the balcony adds +1 but is not marked as a spot; the final meditation may count double (PowerPyx).
disputes.call: Our call: do it in Chapter 1 anyway — free insurance either way.

disputes.topic: How many trophies are hidden on PlayStation?
disputes.call: Our call: 28 — the official list is the arbiter, and the other counts come from pre-launch lists.

disputes.topic: How long does the platinum take?
disputes.call: Our call: budget 200-300 hours; the spread is play style, not a different list.
Our call: both are true — 250 for the trophy, 300 for 100%; the 397 is the total in the game.

disputes.topic: How many challenges in the game?
disputes.call: Our call: 80 exist, 50 earn the trophy, 70 earn 100% — three different thresholds, one list.

disputes.topic: How many shooting ranges are there?
disputes.a: 2 ranges: Griffin (18 golds) and Rodgers Ranch (24 golds) (Push Square, GTABase, WeHunt).
disputes.b: 12 ranges with 42 challenges between them (TheGamesWiki, GTABase trophy tips).
disputes.call: Our call: 2 ranges, 42 challenges — GTABase's own 100% guide names the two ranges and splits the 42 as 18 + 24.

disputes.topic: How many WAiNK locations exist in total?
disputes.b: 112+ across 4 sets: 31 landmarks, 35 curiosities, 23 sculptures, 23 tags (GTAScoop).
disputes.call: Our call: the total is unsettled — but the trophy and 100% both need only 100, so scan 100 and move on.

disputes.topic: How many vehicles does 100% want scanned?
disputes.call: Our call: 200 of 277 base models — standout vehicles do not count, and 277 is the base-model total.

disputes.topic: How many standout vehicles are there?
disputes.b: 281 standout vehicles in 25 categories (TheGamesWiki collectibles page).
disputes.call: Our call: 280-281 — a one-vehicle counting difference; it changes nothing for any trophy.

disputes.topic: How many card sets must be completed?
disputes.call: Our call: both — finish any 3 for the trophy, then keep going to 15 for 100%.

disputes.topic: How many bank vaults, and what do they pay?
disputes.a: 5 vaults for the trophy; 8 vaults exist (PowerPyx).
disputes.b: Vaults pay up to $205,000 each; another guide gives $135,000-$205,000 (GTAScoop).
disputes.call: Our call: 5 of 8 vaults; payouts vary by bank, $135,000-$205,000.
Our call: 8 of 14 — the five named finales plus any three more.

disputes.topic: Which county is the Red Rocks meditation in?
disputes.call: Our call: Manifest Canyon, near where the railroad tracks cross the highway — follow the landmark, not the county label.
